messages:
Sara P: Quick sync — we need a lean playbook for zero-downtime cutovers when we migrate customers to new model versions. 3 main concerns: canary path, customer opt-in/opt-out, and contractual SLAs. 9am PT tomorrow to align?
Mike L: +1. I'd add an explicit perf acceptance gate (p50/p95 latency + token cost delta) before traffic ramp.
Zoe K: Customer comms should include an automated rollback window and a one-click opt-out. Also sample email + FAQ.
Ben O: Rollback triggers I'd suggest: 1) error rate > 0.5% over 5m, 2) p95 increase > 20%, or 3) semantic quality regression on core eval sets. Keep thresholds conservative for enterprise customers.
Ravi M: For models that are quantized or architecture-changed, add compatibility test that runs on a customer's representative prompt set. Can we automate that?
Mike L: We can. Proposal: preflight job that runs small eval set with 'acceptance' criteria. If pass -> canary deploy. If fail -> flag for manual review.
Sara P: Nice. Let's try to keep automated path first, manual only on exceptions. Owners: Mike = infra/canary flow, Zoe = comms + customer opt-in UX, Ben = rollout criteria + SLAs, Ravi = preflight automation.
deploy-bot: Canary created: model=redwood/curie-2026-quant-v2, percent=5, canary_id=cn-179951. Link: https://console.redwood.dev/canaries/cn-179951
Zoe K: Comm timeline: t-minus 48h notice, migration window 2h, 30m customer-level opt-out buffer. Draft email in #marketing, tag for legal review.
Mike L: Operational details (short):
```
# canary ramp script
deploy-canary --model redwood/curie-2026-quant-v2 --start 5 --ramp 5 --checks acceptance,p95,cost
# abort
deploy-canary --abort cn-179951
```
Ben O: Add cost-awareness: if token-cost delta > 12% on a route we keep it pinned and flag finance.
Ravi M: For the preflight automation, sample job outline: 1) run 100 representative prompts, 2) measure entailment score + rouge + latency, 3) fail-fast on quality < baseline - 0.03. Will push a PoC in the morning.
Sara P: Good. Also: contract question — do we need an explicit grace clause for pinned customers so they aren't auto-migrated? Legal asked for opt-in only for enterprise with active pin; otherwise we can auto-swap after 14d. Thoughts?
Zoe K: That matches existing guidance we gave sales. Document the exemption flow and a billing credit if migration causes measurable SLA breach.
Mike L: Ops: add a "compatibility shim" route that maps old API tokens to new model variant for 7d during cutover. Reduces double path handling.
Ben O: Canary observability: require token-level tracing and sample outputs stored for 48h for manual QA. Also record customer-reported quality flags to the rollout dashboard.
Ravi M: One edge-case: models with KV cache incompatibilities — need a migration plan that re-warms caches or keeps old variant until warmed. Call that out in playbook.
Sara P: Action items (short):
- Mike: draft canary runbook + rollback commands by EOD
- Ravi: push preflight PoC + test harness by tomorrow noon
- Zoe: draft comms + opt-out UX + legal note by EOD
- Ben: finalize SLA triggers + observability checklist by tomorrow morning
I'll collate into a single 'zero-downtime cutover' doc and link from the catalog onboarding checklist.
Mike L: SG. I'll include the sample metrics and a short runbook for SRE on-call.
Zoe K: I'll post the comm draft to #marketing in 2h for review. :email:
Ben O: ack :thumbsup:
Ravi M: ack. will include a short CLI for running the preflight locally.
Sara P: Thanks team — meeting confirmed 9am PT. If anything blocks, ping me here or @sara.p.
deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: 2026-05-12T16:00:00Z — playbook sync meeting :)
